lots.title: LOT 5 - Condition Surveys
lots.description: Appointment of a suitably qualified and accredited Chartered Surveying consultancy to deliver a rolling programme of building Condition Surveys for the London Borough of Bexley Residential and Corporate property portfolios (circa 220 street properties and 140 office/community type properties, plus pavilions and a Grade I listed public ceremonial building). The appointed Consultant collects non-intrusive condition data for all main building elements (roof, structure, M&E, decoration, boundary works, etc.), grades them A-D for condition and 1-4 for priority over a 5-year planning horizon, costs remedial works using a recognised schedule of rates, and produces a medium-to-long-term financial plan including backlog maintenance, forward maintenance, and asset life-cycle programmes in accordance with RICS and CIPFA guidance.
requirements: Consultant must be a suitably qualified and accredited Chartered Surveying company delivering condition surveys in accordance with Appendix A, RICS and CIPFA guidance and best practice.
Programme starts on or around 01 September 2026 and runs as a rolling programme aligned to the council's property asset strategy.

Consultant provides an overview of total capital investment requirement and 5-year capital and revenue repair investment plans, broken down by asset/system (e.g. boiler/heating plant, roof, windows) and by building group (e.g. libraries, 2-bedroom dwellings).
Consultant is responsible for programming and managing its own resources to deliver surveys on time and budget, with appropriately trained and qualified staff.
Condition surveys are the detailed inspection of a building and its assets to evaluate deterioration and determine remediation or capital investment required.

Surveys must cover all main elements including: roof covering; internal/external windows and doors; main structure (walls and floors); guttering and chimney stacks; heating and cooling systems; plumbing and sanitary systems; electrical and mechanical equipment; internal/external decoration; boundary walls, fences, gates; car parking and external ground covering.
Consultant coordinates site visits and gives each premises at least three working days' written notice via email; access normally 08:00-17:00 Monday to Friday.
Surveys are non-intrusive visual inspections; intrusive mechanical/electrical surveys are out of scope and separately priced if required.
Each core element and installation photographed and included in report; condition rated A-D (Appendix A); priority rated 1-4 (Appendix A).
Buildings, blocks, floors and rooms numbered in accordance with council-issued site and building plans; AutoCAD-format plans provided where instructed.

Site visits: surveys commence only after appointments are arranged; surveyors wear company ID; report to main office/reception on arrival and departure; follow local site rules; ladders and equipment never left unattended; secure areas not left unattended; site-owned equipment (steps, ladders) not to be used.
Team must include qualified and experienced building surveyors supported by electrical and mechanical engineers and quantity surveyors.

Building Surveyors ideally MRICS qualified or equivalent professional accreditation in building surveying, with building services and maintenance knowledge and current regulation/statutory-compliance knowledge.
Survey data must be collated in a council-provided proforma with dropdown fields and uploaded to the council's property asset management database (CIVICA); this format is non-negotiable.
Alternative data entry via handheld digital device (e.g. Tablet PC) is permitted provided strict quality-control protocols preserve database integrity.

The condition assessments of electrical and mechanical infrastructure are non-intrusive but must identify need for further in-depth inspection/testing; all assessments must comply with current legislation and approved codes of practice.
Consultant collates all property data (name, reference number, construction type, block numbers/names, measured floor areas, location plans, planned works, M&E asset information) prior to survey.
Survey hierarchy: Site -> Building/Property name -> Block -> Floor -> Room; each block identified separately; external areas referenced as Block 0.
Condition grading strictly A (Good), B (Fair), C (Poor), D (Failed) as defined in the specification table.
Priority grading strictly P1 Urgent, P2 Essential (within 2 years), P3 Desirable mid-term (3-5 years), P4 Long Term (>5 years, default for Grade A), applied within a 5-year planning period.

Costings produced using a recognised Schedule of Rates such as BCIS or SPONS pricing matrix and must include preliminaries, preambles, contingencies, site access, site requirements, professional fees, but exclude VAT; costs quoted to bring element up to Grade A or prevailing standard.

Physical access to flat roofs and eaves-level inspection where access is within 3 metres vertical of ground level or fixed permanent access (stairs/ladder) is available; further investigation flagged where defects are apparent or suspected.
A pilot survey on a council-selected site is required; data must be reviewed and accepted before further surveys commence; progressing without acceptance is at Consultant's risk.
Measurements obtained using conventional tapes or electronic devices meeting appropriate industry standards; estimation is not acceptable; dimensions recorded in metric millimetres.
Digital photographs named, numbered and referenced against the data input template, issued in a format to be agreed.
Pre-start site meeting with Council's lead officer required before surveys commence, for induction and approach alignment.
Consultant nominates a senior named person responsible for delivery and maintains in-house quality controls with provision for mid- and post-survey audits.
Consultant produces a dedicated programme for surveying and reporting, updated monthly, with immediate escalation of delays, risks or issues.

Governance: Consultant selects project leads with delegated authority; weekly liaison with Council operational project managers; monthly written project update reports covering progress, upcoming inspections, data-loading progress, risks and issues.

Council may add or omit properties based on strategic acquisitions/disposals, closure/change of use, or Consultant performance; failure against programme may trigger partial or full contract termination.

All survey staff must have completed adequate asbestos awareness training prior to any surveys (particularly residential); each surveyor must consult the on-site Asbestos Management Survey and sign the register before inspection.

Council supplies CAD or line drawings (AutoCAD or PDF) where available; Consultant uses the council's room referencing; if drawings are inaccurate, Consultant notifies the Council and makes amendments at the Schedule-of-Rates rate.

Where no plan is available or PDFs are provided, Consultant prepares new AutoCAD building drawings implementing an agreed building/block/floor/room numbering scheme, with AutoCAD attribute tables and data readable by the asset-management software.

Consultant provides a medium-to-long-term financial plan covering backlog and forward maintenance and a life-cycle/asset-replacement programme aligned to an applicable industry index (RPI, CPI etc.); charged under the Schedule of Rates mechanism.

Indicative minimum life-expectancy baselines: kitchens/kitchenettes/pantries 15 years; bathrooms and toilets (sanitaryware) 20 years; heating systems 20 years; windows and doors 30 years; electrical systems 20 years; pitched roofing 60 years; flat roof (felt) 20 years; water drainage systems 60 years; guttering/facias/soffits, paths/driveways/hardscape, gardens/landscape TBA.

Consultant identifies specific obligations by building type, including but not limited to Energy Performance Certification (EPC/DEC), Asbestos Management (surveys/plans), Electrical Services Certification, Gas Safety, Water Safety, and Fire Safety.

warnings.message: Document is a technical specification for Lot 5 and does not contain explicit tender evaluation criteria or weightings (e.g. MEAT / price-quality split). Any evaluation criteria for this lot are expected in a separate procurement / ITT document rather than this specification.

This specification document does not contain CPV codes for Lot 5; CPV codes are recorded at notice level rather than within the lot-specification body. cpv_codes left empty to avoid unevidenced propagation.

Sections 11, 17 and 18 reference 'Appendix A' for the authoritative condition and priority grading definitions. The extracted markdown contains the inline A-D and P1-P4 definition tables but no standalone 'Appendix A' section; Appendix A is presumed consistent with the inline tables.

Document uses two overlapping numbering schemes: a summary list reusing '1.' for every entry, and a body with numbered headings (1 Overview, 10 Objective, 11 Responsibilities, ...). Body numbering preserved in evidence anchors.
Docling extraction reported page_count=0 for this document; evidence anchors therefore use section identifiers (section:<n>_<slug>) rather than page references.

Governance block in the extract is labelled '21 Governance' with sub-items 21.1-21.4 but appears between sections numbered 26 (Programme) and 27 (Additions/Omissions), suggesting a source-document numbering inconsistency rather than an extraction error.

Lot 5 is a professional surveying services engagement; 'product_requirement_seeds' capture data/drawing/costing/device deliverables rather than physical goods, and may need service-classification handling downstream.

Section 30 contains several 'life expectancy (tba)' placeholders (guttering/facias/soffits, paths/driveways/hardscape, gardens/landscape). Requirements capture the placeholder status rather than implying a specific period.
